title: Frobenius Number — Three Generators with Explicit Formulas

problemStatement.formal: \text{For } a \ge 2 \text{ and } \gcd(a, d) = 1: \ g(a, a+d, a+2d) = \left\lfloor \tfrac{a-2}{2} \right\rfloor \cdot a + (a-1) \cdot d \ (\text{Roberts 1956}).\ \text{Specialization } d=1:\ g(n, n+1, n+2) = \left\lfloor \tfrac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \cdot n + (n-1)\ \text{for } n \ge 3.
problemStatement.plain: Extend the gallery's two-generator Frobenius proof to three generators. The general three-generator problem g(a, b, c) lacks a closed form (Selmer 1977 gave a polynomial-time algorithm, but no explicit formula). However, for STRUCTURED families like arithmetic progressions, three consecutive integers, Fibonacci triples, and Mersenne triples, explicit closed forms ARE known. This entry targets one or more of these special-family closed-form theorems for formalization in Lean, with three-consecutive integers as the natural starting point.
whyMatters: Direct extension of the gallery's flagship 2-generator Frobenius result (frobenius-number-oq-01, verified): each successful 3-generator family adds a worked example to a gap in Mathlib's combinatorics coverage.
Numerical semigroups: the broader theory (Rosales–García-Sánchez monograph 2009) is essentially absent from Mathlib v4.26.0; this entry would seed the worked-examples library.

Concrete bridge from elementary number theory to combinatorics on words / Diophantine analysis: the Apéry-set machinery underlying the Roberts formula is the same machinery used in Selmer's polynomial algorithm and in extremal results on the Sylvester sum.

Catalogue of closed forms for parametric Frobenius families is mature in the literature (Ramírez Alfonsín OUP 2005 monograph collects 70+); a Lean-side translation will be useful both as a Mathlib contribution and as a teaching example.

proven: Roberts (1956): For a ≥ 2 and gcd(a, d) = 1, g(a, a+d, a+2d) = ⌊(a-2)/2⌋·a + (a-1)·d. The k=1 specialization (3 consecutive integers) is g(n, n+1, n+2) = ⌊(n-2)/2⌋·n + (n-1) for n ≥ 3.
Brauer (1942): Same formula for general k-AP — generalizes to g(a, a+d, …, a+kd) = ⌊(a-2)/k⌋·a + (a-1)·d for k ≥ 1, gcd(a,d)=1.
Selmer (1977): Polynomial-time algorithm for g(a, b, c) via Apéry sets, refined by Davison (1994), Killingbergtrø (2000), Beihoffer–Hendry–Nijenhuis–Wagon (2005).
Marín–Ramírez Alfonsín–Revuelta (2007): Closed form for Fibonacci triples g(F_k, F_{k+1}, F_{k+2}), with similar results for Tribonacci.
Brauer–Shockley (1962): General identity g(S) = max Ap(S, a) − a for any a ∈ S, with Ap(S, a) the Apéry set.
Ramírez Alfonsín (1996): The general k-generator Frobenius problem is NP-hard for k ≥ 4.
open: g(a, b, c) for three arbitrary coprime integers — polynomial algorithm exists (Selmer) but no closed-form expression in elementary functions of (a, b, c).
Density and statistics of Frobenius numbers over random tuples (Aliev–Henk–Hinrichs 2011, …).
The Wilf conjecture: relates the Frobenius number, embedding dimension, and number of gaps of a numerical semigroup; open in general.
knownResults.goal: Add a fully verified Lean proof of at least one explicit-formula case for three generators. Minimum-viable target: three-consecutive integers, g(n, n+1, n+2) = ⌊(n-2)/2⌋·n + (n-1) for n ≥ 3. Stretch target: the Roberts 3-AP formula.

currentState.nextAction: S6b ACT — Roberts d=1 tight closed form g(n, n+1, n+2) = floor((n-2)/2)*n + (n-1) for n >= 3, NOW REDUCED to a clean interval-covering argument by S6 ACT (this PR's representable3_consecutive_iff). Paste-ready route (no parity case-split needed for the upper bound): (1) UPPER BOUND — for m > F := floor((n-2)/2)*n + (n-1), set s := m / n; then n*s <= m (Nat.div_mul_le_self / Nat.mul_div_le) and m < n*(s+1) so m <= n*s + (n-1) (Nat.lt_div_add_one_mul_self or Nat.div_add_mod + Nat.mod_lt), and s >= floor((n-2)/2)+1 (from m > F => m/n > F/n = floor((n-2)/2)) gives 2*s >= n-1 (omega on the literal-2 division 2*((n-2)/2) >= n-3), hence m <= n*s + (n-1) <= n*s + 2*s = (n+2)*s; conclude via representable3_consecutive_iff. (2) LOWER BOUND — F itself is non-representable: by representable3_consecutive_iff need to refute exists s, n*s <= F <= (n+2)*s; for s <= floor((n-2)/2): (n+2)*s < n*(s+1) <= ... < F so F > (n+2)*s; for s >= floor((n-2)/2)+1: n*s > F. (3) COMBINE — frobeniusNumber3 n (n+1) (n+2) = F via frobeniusNumber3_le_of_subset_Iio (upper) + not_representable3 + BddAbove (set_non_representable3_finite_of_coprime_ab) (lower, sSup-attained). Est ~50-70 LOC on top of S6. Also queued: S6+ Roberts 3-AP general (a, a+d, a+2d) gcd(a,d)=1; S7+ Fibonacci triples (Marin-Ramirez-Revuelta 2007); S7++ Mersenne triples.

Roberts witness g=(q+1)·n−1 (q=⌊(n-2)/2⌋) is the right end of the LAST gap; intervals [n·s,(n+2)·s] become contiguous at s=q+1 since n≤2(q+1)+1. n=1 is degenerate: g=0 IS representable, so not_representable3_roberts needs n≥2 while the main theorem handles n=1 via the empty non-rep set.

omega understands ℕ floor-division by the literal 2, so ⌊(n-2)/2⌋ bounds (2⌊(n-2)/2⌋ ∈ {n-2,n-3}) are discharged automatically; nonlinear products n·s, (n+2)·s are linked to ⌊(n-2)/2⌋·n by ring-identity `have`s as opaque atoms.

S9 (2026-07-08, researcher-8): The coprimality gcd(a,d)=1 in frobenius_three_ap is NECESSARY, not cosmetic. If g:=gcd(a,d)>=2 then g divides all three AP generators a, a+d, a+2d, hence every representable number; the non-representable set contains the infinite progression {g*k+1} and is infinite — no finite Frobenius number exists.
mathlibGaps: No Mathlib.Combinatorics.NumericalSemigroup module exists at v4.26.0 — neither Frobenius-number generalizations beyond two coprime generators, nor Apéry-set machinery, nor the Brauer–Shockley identity.
Even basic three-generator definitions like sumset {a*x + b*y + c*z : x, y, z ∈ ℕ} have no idiomatic Mathlib spelling; this entry would establish the convention.
The standard Frobenius existence lemma (for gcd(a,b,c) = 1 the non-representable set is finite, hence has a max) is not available in Mathlib — only the 2-generator case via frobeniusNumber_pair.
